        "**IMPACT OF EL NINO- SOUTHERN OSCILLATION(ENSO) ON RAINFALL, HUMIDITY, AND TEMPERATURE IN HYDERABAD(2010-2025): A DATA ANALYSIS USING PYTHON**\n",
        "\n",
        "**ABSTRACT**\n",
        "\n",
        "One of the primary causes of climate variability worldwide is the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), which affects temperature and precipitation patterns in different areas. The relationship between ENSO and specific climate variables in Hyderabad, India, between 2010 and 2025 is examined in this study. NASA POWER provided monthly climate data, including rainfall, humidity, mean temperature, maximum temperature, and minimum temperature; NOAA provided Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) data. Each month was categorized as El Niño, La Niña, or Neutral conditions based on ONI values after the datasets were merged using Python. The impact of ENSO on Hyderabad's climate was assessed using descriptive statistics, bar charts, one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), Tukey's Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) test, and correlation analysis.The findings show statistically significant variations in temperature, humidity, and rainfall between ENSO phases; La Niña showed lower daytime temperatures, while El Niño was often linked to lower humidity and rainfall. Although ENSO affects Hyderabad's climate, other regional and local factors also contribute to climate variability, according to correlation research, which found modest but significant connections between ONI and climatic variables.\n",
        "\n",
        "**INTRODUCTION**\n",
        "\n",
        "Climate variability influences ecosystems, agriculture, water resources, and human livelihoods across the world. The El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a coupled ocean–atmosphere phenomena that originates in the tropical Pacific Ocean, is one of the main causes of interannual climate variability. El Niño, La Niña, and Neutral conditions are the three phases of ENSO that alternate and are distinguished by variations in air circulation and sea surface temperatures.\n",
        "Despite having its origins in the Pacific Ocean, atmospheric teleconnections allow ENSO's effects to spread much beyond the Pacific basin. ENSO has long been related to changes in the southwest monsoon in India, which affects patterns of temperature, humidity, and rainfall distribution. City-level analyses are crucial for comprehending local climate behavior, though, because the form and strength of these relationships frequently differ between places.\n",
        "\n",
        "Hyderabad is situated in southern India's semi-arid Deccan Plateau, and has distinct wet and dry seasons and is impacted by both local climate and monsoonal circulation. Urban planning, water resource management, and climate adaptation can all benefit from an understanding of how ENSO impacts Hyderabad's climate.\n",
        "In this study, monthly climate observations from 2010 to 2025 were analysed using Python to examine the influence of ENSO on rainfall, humidity, and temperature in Hyderabad. To assess variations across ENSO phases and measure the connection between ONI and regional climatic variables, statistical methods such as descriptive analysis, ANOVA, Tukey's HSD test, and correlation analysis were applied."

        "**OBJECTIVES**\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Examination of  the influence of ENSO on rainfall, humidity,and temperature in Hyderabad between 2010 and 2025.\n",
        "2. Classification of monthly climate obsrvations into El Nino. La Nina, and neutral phases using the Oceanc Nino Index(ONI).\n",
        "3. Comparison of climatic variables across different ENSO phases using statistical methods.\n",
        "4. Investigation of correlation between ONI and selected climate variables.\n",
        "5. Demonstration of the application of Python in climate data processing, visualization and statistical analysis.\n",
        "\n",
        "**STUDY AREA**\n",
        "\n",
        "Hyderabad, located in the state of Telagana,India,lies at 17.36°N latitude and 78.48°E longitude. The city experiences a tropical semi-arid climate characterised by hot summers, a southwest monsoon season and mild winters.\n",
        "\n",
        "**DATA SOURCES**\n",
        "\n",
        "Two datasets were used in ths study:\n",
        "\n",
        "CLIMATE DATA\n",
        "\n",
        "Source: NASA POWER\n",
        "Period: January 2010-December 2025\n",
        "Variables:\n",
        "\n",
        "*   Monthly Rainfall\n",
        "*   Relative Humidity\n",
        "*   Mean Temperature\n",
        "*   Maximum Temperature\n",
        "*   Minimum Temperature\n",
        "\n",
        "ENSO DATA\n",
        "Source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center\n",
        "Dataset: Oceanic Nino Index(ONI)\n",
        "Period: January 2010-December 2025\n",
        "\n",
        "**METHODOLOGY**\n",
        "\n",
        "1.DATA PREPARATION\n",
        "\n",
        "NASA POWER was used to import climate data.\n",
        "NOAA's ONI data was translated from wide format to long format.\n",
        "To ensure interoperability between datasets, year and month fields were standardized.\n",
        "\n",
        "2. DATA NTEGRATION\n",
        "\n",
        "The common variables Year and Month were used to combine the climate and ONI datasets.\n",
        "Every climatic observation was given a monthly ONI value.\n",
        "\n",
        "3. ENSO CLASSIFICATION\n",
        "\n",
        " The Oceanic Niño Index was used to categorize monthly observations into three ENSO phases:\n",
        " El Niño: ONI >= +0.5\n",
        " La Niña: ONI ≤ –0.5\n",
        " Neutral: ONI < +0.5 < –0.5\n",
        "\n",
        " 4. EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS\n",
        "\n",
        " For every ENSO phase, the mean values of rainfall, humidity, mean temperature, maximum temperature, and minimum temperature were computed.\n",
        " To compare climatic factors throughout ENSO periods, bar charts and subplot visualizations were created.\n",
        "\n",
        " 5. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS\n",
        "\n",
        "ANOVA, or one-way analysis of variance, was used to assess whether climatic variables varied significantly between ENSO phases.\n",
        "When ANOVA revealed statistically significant differences, Tukey's Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) test was carried out.\n",
        "\n",
        "6. CORRELATION ANALYSIS\n",
        "\n",
        "The ONI and climatic factors were compared using Pearson correlation coefficients.\n",
        "A correlation heatmap was created to show the connections between temperature, humidity, rainfall, and ONI."

              "function _uploadFiles(inputId, outputId) {\n",
              "  const steps = uploadFilesStep(inputId, outputId);\n",
              "  const outputElement = document.getElementById(outputId);\n",
              "  // Cache steps on the outputElement to make it available for the next call\n",
              "  // to uploadFilesContinue from Python.\n",
              "  outputElement.steps = steps;\n",
              "\n",
              "  return _uploadFilesContinue(outputId);\n",
              "}\n",
              "\n",
              "// This is roughly an async generator (not supported in the browser yet),\n",
              "// where there are multiple asynchronous steps and the Python side is going\n",
              "// to poll for completion of each step.\n",
              "// This uses a Promise to block the python side on completion of each step,\n",
              "// then passes the result of the previous step as the input to the next step.\n",
              "function _uploadFilesContinue(outputId) {\n",
              "  const outputElement = document.getElementById(outputId);\n",
              "  const steps = outputElement.steps;\n",
              "\n",
              "  const next = steps.next(outputElement.lastPromiseValue);\n",
              "  return Promise.resolve(next.value.promise).then((value) => {\n",
              "    // Cache the last promise value to make it available to the next\n",
              "    // step of the generator.\n",
              "    outputElement.lastPromiseValue = value;\n",
              "    return next.value.response;\n",
              "  });\n",
              "}\n",
              "\n",
              "/**\n",
              " * Generator function which is called between each async step of the upload\n",
              " * process.\n",
              " * @param {string} inputId Element ID of the input file picker element.\n",
              " * @param {string} outputId Element ID of the output display.\n",
              " * @return {!Iterable<!Object>} Iterable of next steps.\n",
              " */\n",
              "function* uploadFilesStep(inputId, outputId) {\n",
              "  const inputElement = document.getElementById(inputId);\n",
              "  inputElement.disabled = false;\n",
              "\n",
              "  const outputElement = document.getElementById(outputId);\n",
              "  outputElement.innerHTML = '';\n",
              "\n",
              "  const pickedPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {\n",
              "    inputElement.addEventListener('change', (e) => {\n",
              "      resolve(e.target.files);\n",
              "    });\n",
              "  });\n",
              "\n",
              "  const cancel = document.createElement('button');\n",
              "  inputElement.parentElement.appendChild(cancel);\n",
              "  cancel.textContent = 'Cancel upload';\n",
              "  const cancelPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {\n",
              "    cancel.onclick = () => {\n",
              "      resolve(null);\n",
              "    };\n",
              "  });\n",
              "\n",
              "  // Wait for the user to pick the files.\n",
              "  const files = yield {\n",
              "    promise: Promise.race([pickedPromise, cancelPromise]),\n",
              "    response: {\n",
              "      action: 'starting',\n",
              "    }\n",
              "  };\n",
              "\n",
              "  cancel.remove();\n",
              "\n",
              "  // Disable the input element since further picks are not allowed.\n",
              "  inputElement.disabled = true;\n",
              "\n",
              "  if (!files) {\n",
              "    return {\n",
              "      response: {\n",
              "        action: 'complete',\n",
              "      }\n",
              "    };\n",
              "  }\n",
              "\n",
              "  for (const file of files) {\n",
              "    const li = document.createElement('li');\n",
              "    li.append(span(file.name, {fontWeight: 'bold'}));\n",
              "    li.append(span(\n",
              "        `(${file.type || 'n/a'}) - ${file.size} bytes, ` +\n",
              "        `last modified: ${\n",
              "            file.lastModifiedDate ? file.lastModifiedDate.toLocaleDateString() :\n",
              "                                    'n/a'} - `));\n",
              "    const percent = span('0% done');\n",
              "    li.appendChild(percent);\n",
              "\n",
              "    outputElement.appendChild(li);\n",
              "\n",
              "    const fileDataPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {\n",
              "      const reader = new FileReader();\n",
              "      reader.onload = (e) => {\n",
              "        resolve(e.target.result);\n",
              "      };\n",
              "      reader.readAsArrayBuffer(file);\n",
              "    });\n",
              "    // Wait for the data to be ready.\n",
              "    let fileData = yield {\n",
              "      promise: fileDataPromise,\n",
              "      response: {\n",
              "        action: 'continue',\n",
              "      }\n",
              "    };\n",
              "\n",
              "    // Use a chunked sending to avoid message size limits. See b/62115660.\n",
              "    let position = 0;\n",
              "    do {\n",
              "      const length = Math.min(fileData.byteLength - position, MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE);\n",
              "      const chunk = new Uint8Array(fileData, position, length);\n",
              "      position += length;\n",
              "\n",
              "      const base64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode.apply(null, chunk));\n",
              "      yield {\n",
              "        response: {\n",
              "          action: 'append',\n",
              "          file: file.name,\n",
              "          data: base64,\n",
              "        },\n",
              "      };\n",
              "\n",
              "      let percentDone = fileData.byteLength === 0 ?\n",
              "          100 :\n",
              "          Math.round((position / fileData.byteLength) * 100);\n",
              "      percent.textContent = `${percentDone}% done`;\n",
              "\n",
              "    } while (position < fileData.byteLength);\n",
              "  }\n",
              "\n",
              "  // All done.\n",
              "  yield {\n",
              "    response: {\n",
              "      action: 'complete',\n",
              "    }\n",

        "import pandas as pd\n",
        "rainfall_long = rainfall.melt(\n",
        "    id_vars=[\"YEAR\"],\n",
        "    value_vars= [\"JAN\",\"FEB\",\"MAR\",\"APR\",\"MAY\",\"JUN\",\"JUL\",\"AUG\",\"SEP\",\"OCT\",\"NOV\",\"DEC\"],\n",
        "    var_name=\"MONTH\",\n",
        "    value_name=\"RAINFALL\"\n",
        ")\n",
        "month_order=[\n",
        "    \"JAN\",\"FEB\",\"MAR\",\"APR\",\"MAY\",\"JUN\",\"JUL\",\"AUG\",\"SEP\",\"OCT\",\"NOV\",\"DEC\"\n",
        "]\n",
        "rainfall_long[\"MONTH\"]= pd.Categorical(\n",
        "    rainfall_long[\"MONTH\"],\n",
        "    categories= month_order,\n",
        "    ordered= True\n",
        ")\n",
        "rainfall_long= rainfall_long.sort_values(\n",
        "    by=[\"YEAR\",\"MONTH\"]\n",
        ")\n",
        "rainfall_long = rainfall_long.reset_index(drop=True)\n",
        "rainfall_long.head(15)\n",
        "def convert_to_long (parameter_name, new_column_name):\n",
        "    filtered= df[df[\"PARAMETER\"]== parameter_name]\n",
        "    long_df = filtered.melt(\n",
        "      id_vars=[\"YEAR\"],\n",
        "      value_vars = [\"JAN\",\"FEB\",\"MAR\",\"APR\",\"MAY\",\"JUN\",\"JUL\",\"AUG\",\"SEP\",\"OCT\",\"NOV\",\"DEC\"],\n",
        "      var_name = \"MONTH\",\n",
        "      value_name = new_column_name\n",
        "    )\n",
        "    month_order=[\"JAN\",\"FEB\",\"MAR\",\"APR\",\"MAY\",\"JUN\",\"JUL\",\"AUG\",\"SEP\",\"OCT\",\"NOV\",\"DEC\"]\n",
        "\n",
        "    long_df[\"MONTH\"]= pd.Categorical(\n",
        "    long_df[\"MONTH\"],\n",
        "     categories=month_order,\n",
        "     ordered=True\n",
        "    )\n",
        "    long_df= long_df.sort_values(\n",
        "    by=[\"YEAR\",\"MONTH\"]\n",
        "    )\n",
        "    long_df = long_df.reset_index(drop=True)\n",
        "    return long_df\n",
        "rainfall= convert_to_long(\"PRECTOTCORR_SUM\",\"RAINFALL\")\n",
        "print(rainfall.head())\n",
        "humidity= convert_to_long(\"RH2M\",\"HUMIDITY\")\n",

        "temperature= convert_to_long(\"T2M\",\"TEMPERATURE\")\n",
        "print(temperature.head())\n",
        "temperature_max= convert_to_long(\"T2M_MAX\", \"TEMPERATURE_MAX\")\n",
        "print(temperature_max.head())\n",
        "temperature_min= convert_to_long(\"T2M_MIN\", \"TEMPERATURE_MIN\")\n",

      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "import pandas as pd\n",
        "month_map= {\n",
        "    \"JAN\":1,\"FEB\":2,\"MAR\":3,\"APR\":4,\"MAY\":5,\"JUN\":6,\n",
        "    \"JUL\":7,\"AUG\":8,\"SEP\":9,\"OCT\":10,\"NOV\":11,\"DEC\":12\n",
        "}\n",
        "climate[\"MONTH_NUM\"]=climate[\"MONTH\"].map(month_map)\n",
        "\n",
        "climate[\"PERIOD\"]=pd.PeriodIndex.from_fields(\n",
        "    year=climate[\"YEAR\"],\n",
        "    month=climate[\"MONTH_NUM\"],\n",
        "    freq=\"M\"\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "climate.head()\n",
        "climate= climate.drop(columns=[\"MONTH_NUM\"])\n",
        "cols= [\"PERIOD\"]+ [col for col in climate.columns if col!= \"PERIOD\"]#removing column period and then adding period column to the new list without column and saving it to cols\n",
        "climate= climate[cols]#first col creates a new list, adding elements to it;whereas the second col is a regular loop, it iterates through every column and checks. if the column is not period, it keeps the column ad adds it to the newly created list\n",
        "climate.head()\n"
      ],

        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
        "import numpy as np\n",
        "def plot_histogram(column,title,xlabel,color): #code for all histograms\n",
        "    counts,bins,patches = plt.hist(\n",
        "    climate[column],\n",
        "    bins=10,\n",
        "    color=color,\n",
        "    edgecolor=\"black\"\n",
        "  )\n",
        "    plt.title(title,fontsize=15)\n",
        "    plt.xlabel(xlabel)\n",
        "    plt.ylabel(\"Frequency\")\n",
        "    plt.grid(axis=\"y\",alpha=0.3)\n",
        "\n",
        "    for count,patch in zip(counts,patches):\n",
        "        plt.text(\n",
        "        patch.get_x()+ patch.get_width()/2,#label for x-axis,1.gets left edge and get_width gives width of the bar\n",
        "        count+ 0.5, # gets y coordinate\n",
        "        int(count),\n",
        "        ha=\"center\",\n",
        "        fontsize=10\n",
        "        )\n",
        "    mean= climate[column].mean()\n",
        "    plt.axvline(\n",
        "        mean,\n",
        "        color=\"red\",\n",
        "        linestyle=\"--\",\n",
        "        linewidth=2,\n",
        "        label=f\"mean={mean:.1f}\"\n",
        "        )\n",
        "    median=climate[column].median()\n",
        "    plt.axvline(\n",
        "        median,\n",
        "        color=\"green\",\n",
        "        linestyle=\"--\",\n",
        "        linewidth=2,\n",
        "        label=f\"median={median:.1f}\"\n",
        "        )\n",
        "    plt.legend()\n",
        "    plt.show() #inside the function\n",
        "plot_histogram( #Filling the parameters\n",
        "        \"HUMIDITY\",\n",
        "        \"DISTRIBUTION OF MONTHLY HUMIDITY\",\n",
        "        \"HUMIDITY(%)\",\n",
        "        \"blue\"\n",

        "#SUMMARY STATISTICS"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "W_3ZMNTdLXeE"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "#import ANOVA Function\n",
        "from scipy.stats import f_oneway\n",
        "el_nino=merged_climate[merged_climate[\"ENSO_phase\"]==\"El Nino\"][\"RAINFALL\"]\n",
        "la_nina=merged_climate[merged_climate[\"ENSO_phase\"]==\"La Nina\"][\"RAINFALL\"]\n",
        "neutral=merged_climate[merged_climate[\"ENSO_phase\"]==\"Neutral\"][\"RAINFALL\"]\n"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "W3XeDfDgdZJ_"
      },
      "execution_count": null,
      "outputs": []
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "F_statistic, p_value = f_oneway(\n",
        "    el_nino,\n",
        "    la_nina,\n",
        "    neutral\n",
        ")\n",
        "print(f\"F-statistic: {F_statistic}\")\n",
        "print(f\"P-value:{p_value}\")\n",
        "\n",
        "if p_value <=0.05:\n",
        "  print(\"Rainfall differs significantly among ENSO phases.\")\n",
        "else:\n",

        "F, p = f_oneway(el_nino, la_nina, neutral)\n",
        "\n",

        "\n",
        "if p < 0.05:\n",
        "    tukey = pairwise_tukeyhsd(\n",

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "**DISCUSSION**\n",
        "\n",
        "The study shows that ENSO has an impact on Hyderabads climate. The effect varies among different climate variables. Monthly rainfall differed significantly during ENSO phases. When there is El Niño, the city gets the lowest average rainfall and when it is Neutral it gets the highest. This finding is consistent with the well-established notion that El Niño is known to make the Indian summer monsoon weaker, which reduces rainfall in many parts of India.\n",
        "\n",
        "The humidity also showed significant variation during ENSO phases. La Nina months exhibited the highest average humidity, whereas El Nino recorded the lowest. Increased humidity is likely associated with enhanced monsoonal activity and greater moisture availability.\n",
        "\n",
        "Temperature variables showed contrasting responses. Mean and maximum temperatures were lower during La Nina conditions, while neutral phase recorded the highest average temperatures. Tukey's HSD analysis confirmed these statistic differences.\n",
        "\n",
        "Correlation analysis revealed only weak relationships between ONI and individual variable. Although El Nino tended to reduce rainfall and humidity, the relatively low correlation coefficients. Regional atmospheric circulation, local weather systems, urban heat sland and seasonal monsoon variability likely contribute substantially to climatic conditions in the city.\n",
        "\n",
        "The findings indicate that ENSO has a measurable influence on Hyderabad's climate, but variability in local climate results from the combined effects of interacting factors.\n"

        "**CONCLUSION**\n",
        "\n",
        "This study evaluated monthly observations from 2010 to 2025 to investigate how the El Niño–Southern Oscillation affected Hyderabad's climate. Temperature, humidity, and rainfall fluctuated considerably between ENSO phases, as shown by statistical analysis. While La Niña situations showed lower daytime temperatures, El Niño conditions were typically linked to less rainfall and humidity. According to correlation research, ONI had weak but significant connections with climatic variables, suggesting that ENSO is not the only factor influencing Hyderabad's climate variability.\n",
        "Additionally, the study shows how Python may be used for statistical analysis, processing, and visualization of climate data. The project's process can be expanded to look into longer observational records, other climatic variables, or other Indian cities.\n",
        "\n",
        "**LIMITATIONS**\n",
        "\n",
        "* The study considered only one city.\n",
        "* Only five climatic variables were analysed.\n",
        "* Other large scale climate drivers such as the Indian Ocean Dipole(IOD), MJO were not included.\n",
        "* Correlation analysis identifies associations but does not establish causal relationships.\n",
